initial_observation.demographics: 20 years old patient trader resident in Senegal with no known medical history
initial_observation.encounter_context: admitted on August 2015 in the Neurology Department of Fann National Teaching Hospital
initial_observation.chief_complaint: abrupt onset of left body side weakness five days before admission
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: weakness preceded by acute headaches and rotatory vertigo without nausea or vomiting
presenting_symptoms: rotatory vertigo without nausea or vomiting

evidence_items.source_text: Physical examination found paralysis of right oculomotor movements, right facial palsy, and left hemiparesis sparing the face which constitute the superior pons type of Foville syndrome.
The brain CT scan shown spontaneous hemorrhage in the right pontine’s posterolateral part compressing the fourth ventricle
Patient received antalgic, anxiolytic, laxative and physiotherapy as treatment with clinical improvement. And he has been discharge 10 days later.
We report a case of superior Foville syndrome due to a pontine hemorrhage in a young patient.
